evals.name: dashboard-from-scratch
evals.prompt: I'm building an internal ops dashboard in React. Need a page with a top nav, a left sidebar, and a 4-across row of metric tiles showing request rate, error rate, p99 latency and uptime, then a table of recent deployments below it. It has to support dark mode. Set up the project styling too.
evals.expected_output: Uses @carbon/react with the UI Shell (HeaderContainer/Header/SideNav/Content), Grid+Column with condensed for the tile row, DataTable for deployments, GlobalTheme or Theme for dark mode, spacing/type/theme tokens rather than raw values, and wires the SCSS entry point plus IBM Plex.

assertions.text: Imports components from @carbon/react, not carbon-components-react
Uses the UI Shell components rather than a hand-built header/sidebar
Uses Grid and Column with per-breakpoint props for the tile row
Uses DataTable rather than a raw <table>
Contains no raw hex color codes in the styling it writes
Contains no raw px values for padding/margin/gap
Applies type via type-style() or a Carbon type token, not bare font-size
Sets up theming with Theme/GlobalTheme rather than a CSS class alone
Mentions installing sass and loading IBM Plex

evals.name: audit-existing-frontend
evals.prompt: we inherited this react app from a contractor and leadership wants it 'on carbon' by q4. can you look at src/ and tell me how far off we actually are, and what to do first? i need something i can put in front of a VP.
evals.expected_output: Runs detection commands, scores the six dimensions with evidence, produces the structured gap-analysis report with severities, file:line citations, effort estimates, and a prioritized sequence. Does not start editing code.

assertions.text: Measures before changing anything (does not begin editing files)
Scores across the six dimensions (foundation, tokens, components, layout, theming, accessibility)
Cites concrete file paths and line numbers as evidence
Assigns severity levels to findings
Produces a prioritized sequence rather than an unordered list
Puts a short summary before the detail (VP-readable)

evals.name: token-choice
evals.prompt: quick one — I have a settings panel that sits inside a card on our main page. inside the panel there's a form with a few text inputs and a divider between sections. what background/border should each of those be? we support light and dark.
evals.expected_output: Card is layer-01, panel wrapped in <Layer> so it resolves to layer-02 (or uses the contextual $layer token), inputs use $field-* not $layer-*, divider uses $border-subtle-*, input outline uses $border-strong-*. Explains that the layer number is nesting depth, not a shade.

assertions.text: Recommends $field-* for input backgrounds, not $layer-*
Recommends $border-subtle-* for the divider
Uses <Layer> or the contextual $layer token rather than hand-picking $layer-02
Explains that layer numbers encode nesting depth, not lightness
Names no raw hex values as the answer

evals.name: vue-version-trap
evals.prompt: starting a new vue 3 admin tool at work and we're supposed to use carbon since that's the company standard. what do I install and how do I set up theming? want the g100 dark theme.
evals.expected_output: Flags that @carbon/vue targets Carbon v10 (not v11) and lacks a g100-equivalent token set matching v11, recommends @carbon/web-components for a new Vue 3 project, and gives the isCustomElement config plus the theme setup.

assertions.text: Identifies that @carbon/vue targets Carbon v10, not v11
Recommends @carbon/web-components as the better path for new Vue 3 work
Provides the Vue compilerOptions.isCustomElement config for cds- tags
Shows theming via @carbon/styles theme mixin or custom properties
Does not silently give v11 token names for a v10 library

evals.name: ai-summary-surface
evals.prompt: we're adding an AI-generated summary at the top of each incident page. it should look distinct from the rest of the page so people know a model wrote it, and they should be able to see why it said what it said. react + carbon.
evals.expected_output: Uses AILabel with real explanatory AILabelContent and AILabelActions, attaches it via the decorator prop on a Tile with hasRoundedCorners, references ai-* tokens, uses AISkeleton while generating, and does not invent a confidence number.

assertions.text: Uses AILabel (not the deprecated Slug)
Attaches it with the decorator prop (not the deprecated slug prop)
Puts substantive explanatory content inside AILabelContent
Uses an AI skeleton for the generating state
Does not apply the AI treatment to non-AI parts of the page
